title: Second Mexican Empire
capsule: The Second Mexican Empire was proclaimed in 1863 when French forces under Napoleon III, invited by Mexican conservatives, occupied Mexico City and offered the crown to Austrian Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg, who arrived in Veracruz in May 1864. Maximilian's liberal inclinations — he confirmed the Reform Laws on Church property and religious freedom — alienated the conservative faction that had sponsored him, while Benito Juárez's republican forces never ceased resistance. Following the American Civil War, U.S. diplomatic pressure compelled Napoleon III to withdraw French troops by early 1867; left with a shrunken loyal force, Maximilian was besieged at Querétaro, betrayed from within, and captured in May 1867. He was court-martialed and executed on 19 June 1867 alongside generals Mejía and Miramón, restoring the republic under Juárez.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial control was never uniform: the empire's effective reach fluctuated with French troop deployments and republican resistance, making any single boundary map a significant simplification.
